name: Schwimmen
description: Schwimmen (31) is a Commerce-group card game in which players hold three cards and improve their hand by exchanging with a central pool of three face-up cards. The aim is to collect cards of one suit totalling as high as possible (maximum 31) or three of a kind. Played with chips; the loser of each hand loses a chip and the last survivor wins. Popular in Germany and Austria.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Austria and Germany (particularly western Austria and Germany). Known in many parts of the world.
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional card games in the region; German name Schwimmen (swimming) refers to the last chance before a player drops out.
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Austria and Germany
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional
setup.deck:
Type: 32-card deck (strip 2-6 from standard pack). Cards 7-10, J, Q, K, A in four suits. One deck.
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
setup.dealing: Dealer gives 3 cards face down to each player plus one extra hand of 3 cards. Dealer chooses to keep their own 3 or the extra hand (before seeing the extra hand). The rejected 3 cards are turned face up and placed in the centre as the table pool. Dealing pattern: clockwise.
setup.equipment:
32-card deck (or strip 2-6 from standard deck)
Chips or tokens (e.g. 3 per player)
Table space

rules.objective: Have the highest-scoring three-card hand at the end of a hand (same-suit total, max 31, or three of a kind). Avoid losing chips; be the last player with chips to win the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Setup: Each player receives chips (e.g. 3 each). Deal 3 cards each plus dealer's extra hand; dealer's rejected 3 form the table pool.
2. Play: Player to dealer's left acts first; turn passes clockwise. On your turn you may: (a) exchange one card with one table card, (b) exchange all three hand cards for the three table cards, or (c) pass. You may not exchange exactly two cards.
3. Special combinations: Feuer (three aces = 32) or Schnauz (31 in one suit) must be exposed immediately and the hand ends.
4. If all pass in succession, replace the three table cards with three from the talon and continue.
5. A player may close at end of turn; then each other player gets one more turn and the hand ends.
6. Scoring: Expose hands. Score = sum of one suit (or three of a kind: 30.5, except three aces = 32). Worst hand loses one chip. Feuer: all except holder lose a chip. Last chip lost = swimming; one more loss and you drop out. Last survivor wins.
keyRules: Exchange one card, all three, or pass; never exchange exactly two
Feuer (three aces) and Schnauz (31 in one suit) end the hand immediately
Lowest hand loses one chip; Feuer makes all others lose one chip
Player who loses last chip is swimming; next loss eliminates them

strategy.basic: Improve your hand by swapping with the table; aim for 31 in one suit or three of a kind. Do not show reaction when someone takes a card you needed.
strategy.intermediate: Assume each player gets about three turns before someone closes. Form a plan and a backup (e.g. aim for three nines; if a nine is taken, switch to improving suit total). Watch which cards opponents take and discard to infer their targets.
strategy.advanced: Misdirect by staring at an unwanted card. If you must leave a high card, choose one that helps an opponent least. When swapping all three, opponents know your point total for the rest of the hand.
tips: Do not stare at the card you need; opponents will notice
Games rarely last more than three rounds before someone closes
Deduce opponents' strategies from their exchanges

variations.name: Dutch 31
variations.description: You must exchange or close each turn (no pass). Closing does not end the hand; play continues until only two remain, then one may close. Declaring 31 ends the hand immediately. No Feuer; three aces score 30.5. Often scored with dice (start at 6); first to 0 gets the Chicken (one extra life).
